ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Hippocrates

code.originalText: Four-month review: knee function, repeat gait, balance and strength measures, vitamin D, falls and the home program

text.paragraph: Hippocrates finished twelve weeks of physical therapy and goes to tai chi twice a week. He walks into town for his teaching and stops once on the hill. His knees ache at 2 of 10 on the hill; he uses the gel most mornings and acetaminophen two or three times a week. He has had no falls and no dizziness. He takes vitamin D3 daily. He had the RSV and first zoster vaccines three weeks ago with a sore arm for a day. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-29; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 132/72 seated and 130/72 standing; pulse 64; weight 64.6 kg
Both knees: crepitus, no effusion; quadriceps 5 of 5 on the right, 4+ of 5 on the left
Rises from a chair without his arms; turns steadily

Slower walking, knee pain on stairs and one near-fall in the past six months, found on the comprehensive geriatric assessment at intake: gait speed 0.78 m/s, Timed Up and Go 13.8 seconds, unable to hold a tandem stance for 10 seconds, grip 24 kg; cause under evaluation with a geriatric medicine consultation

S — Synthetic presenting problem of normal aging found on a comprehensive geriatric assessment; superseded at the consultation, when knee osteoarthritis with reduced leg strength and balance was diagnosed.

Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, diagnosed clinically by the ACR criteria (knee pain, age over 50, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, crepitus, bony enlargement, no warmth), with reduced quadriceps strength and balance and an increased risk of falls; KOOS JR 62
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation: a common, mild condition of aging chosen for a figure with no documented illness; not a claim about his real knees.
Potentially inappropriate over-the-counter medicines (Beers 2023): naproxen most days for about two years and diphenhydramine for sleep three or four nights a week; both stopped at intake
S — Synthetic medication history found on the deprescribing review.
Low bone mass (femoral neck T-score -1.7, total hip -1.4) with vitamin D insufficiency (24 ng/mL); FRAX 10-year risk 11 percent major and 2.6 percent hip, below treatment thresholds
S — Synthetic DXA finding at eight weeks; not a claim about his real bones.

Common cold (viral upper respiratory infection) with runny nose, sore throat and a mild cough, no fever, chest clear, oxygen saturation 97 percent; COVID-19 and influenza tests negative; resolved in about ten days
S — Synthetic acute illness; not a historical claim.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Age-Friendly Health Systems: the 4Ms (What Matters, Medication, Mentation, Mobility) (2026); American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults (2023); Updating STEADI for Primary Care: Recommendations From the American Geriatrics Society Workgroup (2025); World guidelines for falls prevention and management for older adults: a global initiative (2022); Physical Frailty: ICFSR International Clinical Practice Guidelines for Identification and Management (2019); 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); The clinician's guide to prevention and treatment of osteoporosis (2022); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis, and osteoporosis monographs (2026)

Follow-up: Seven-month review in three months with the second zoster dose and the influenza vaccine. The clinic for any fall. Next scheduled visit 2026-09-28: seven-month review: knee function, mobility, falls, medicines, vaccines and what matters most to him. [S]
